item.title: Own goal helps Brighton & Hove Albion record victory at Everton
item.description: Own goal helps Brighton & Hove Albion record victory at Everton A Maz Pacheco own goal helped Brighton & Hove Albion to record a 1-0 victory over Everton at Goodison Park on Sunday afternoon. Pacheco put through her own net after just six minutes as the visitors ended the second block of matches with a win. Olivia García created an early chance for Brighton & Hove Albion. She passed the ball to captain Maisie Symonds, but she sent her effort wide. Pacheco then netted an own goal when her back-pass deceived both Rion Ishikawa and Courtney Brosnan and the ball rolled into the goal. Brighton & Hove Albion searched for a second goal. A ball was played through by Lily Murphy towards Kiko Seike, but her touch wasn’t enough and it was caught well by Brosnan. Fran Kirby then played the ball to Seike, but Ishikawa timed her run perfectly and intercepted the ball. Ornella Vignola almost found an equaliser for Everton. She attempted to whip the ball towards the far corner, but her shot went just wide. Hannah Blundell was then in on goal, but her shot was saved by Chiamaka Nnadozie. Jutta Rantala was next to have a chance in the box, but her effort was blocked. Brighton & Hove Albion went close when Marisa Olislagers struck the ball from range, but Brosnan got her finger tips to it as the game ended 1-0 in The Seagulls’ favour. This afternoon’s result sees Brighton & Hove Albion go to seventh place in the Barclays Women’s Super League table while Everton drop to 11th.

item.title: Bremen thrash Hamburg in derby, Augsburg win with Gregoritsch's brace
item.description: Hamburg's Miro Muheim battles for the ball with Werder Bremen's Ludovit Reis during German Bundesliga soccer match between Werder Bremen and Hamburger SV at the Weserstadion. (is associated with: «Bremen thrash Hamburg in derby, Augsburg win with Gregoritsch's brace») Carmen Jaspersen/dpa Werder Bremen lit up in the second half, with Justin Njinmah scoring a brace, to thrash Hamburg 4-0 in the Bundesliga Northern derby on Sunday. After a goalless first half, Bremen captain Marco Friedl broke the deadlock in the 55th minute. Goalkeeper Daniel Heuer Fernandes parried his first effort after a corner, but the ball returned to the skipper, who didn't miss the second chance and hit a powerful volley into the net. Njinmah then found the net twice, in the 66th and then in 70th, before fan favourite Niclas Füllkrug sealed the victory with a stunner in stoppage time. "Clear derby win, 4-0. We can all go back home happy today," Njinmah told broadcasters DAZN. Bremen, who finished the previous season just three points above the relegation zone, are having a good campaign so far and are sixth in the table, while Hamburg are 12th. Earlier, Michael Gregoritsch also scored a brace to lead Augsburg to a 3-1 win against Mainz. The Austrian forward broke the deadlock for the hosts in the 19th minute. Yannik Keitel's effort from a corner was kept out by goalkeeper Robin Zentner, but Gregoritsch poked the rebound home. Juma Bah made it 2-0 in the 36th from a similar situation. Zentner again stopped the initial attempt after a corner, but the loose ball fell to Bah, who fired it into the net. Keitel thought he had a third, but the goal was ruled out due to a foul. Augsburg coach Manuel Baum was frustrated with the decision and had a confrontation with Nadiem Amiri as he refused to return the ball. Baum was sent off, while Amiri received a yellow card. The incident didn't seem to affect the Augsburg players and Gregoritsch scored another goal early in the second half. A free-kick was initially cleared by the Mainz defence, but the ball was returned to the area. It looped in the air before bouncing off the back of Stefan Posch's head and into the path of Gregoritsch, who volleyed it home in the 48th. Ransford-Yeboah Königsdörffer pulled one back for Mainz three minutes later but couldn't threaten a comeback. Augsburg moved up to 10th, while Mainz dropped to 13th. "Today we not only defended well, but also played really well with the ball. Especially with the unfamiliar defensive line-up, the team handled it brilliantly – a huge compliment to them," Baum said. Bayern Munich were held to a 1-1 draw by Cologne on Friday, which opened the door for Borussia Dortmund to take the Bundesliga lead after a 1-0 win against Borussia Mönchengladbach on Saturday. item.title: Manchester United humbled at Liverpool on Pochettino’s debut as boss
item.description: Manchester United manager Mauricio Pochettino gestures on the touchline during the English Premier League soccer match between Liverpool and Manchester United at the Anfield. (is associated with: «Manchester United humbled at Liverpool on Pochettino’s debut as boss») Martin Rickett/PA Wire/dpa Mauricio Pochettino’s Manchester United reign got off to a miserable start as Liverpool punished Leny Yoro’s red card with a pair of early goals on their way to a comprehensive 4-0 win against their relegation-threatened rivals. A whirlwind week for the former Argentina international ended in all too familiar disappointment for the faltering Red Devils, whose hopes of enjoying a new manager bounce were extinguished within 13 nightmare minutes at Anfield. Dominik Szoboszlai’s fierce free-kick put Liverpool ahead after United defender Yoro was sent off for denying a goalscoring opportunity and Florian Wirtz’s smart finish quickly put Pochettino’s side further behind. United temporarily stemmed the tide thanks to some last-ditch defending, wayward finishing and key Senne Lammens stops, but Andoni Iraola’s Reds redoubled their efforts in the second half. In truth, Pochettino’s 10 men were fortunate that Liverpool only added a further two goals though Rio Ngumoha and substitute Victor Munoz, such was their dominance. Iraola’s side end the weekend in fourth whereas United languish 19th in the standings as their winless Premier League run stretched to a ninth match and attention now turns to Wednesday’s Champions League trip to Sporting.

item.title: Baltimore Ravens’ Other Trade Offer for Former First-Round QB Revealed
item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Baltimore Ravens’ season went off the rails when Lamar Jackson suffered a dislocated thumb on his right hand, knocking him out for an extended stretch, if not the rest of the year. The Ravens’ general manager Eric DeCosta responded by trading for 11-year veteran Jacoby Brissett. While the Ravens have a new quarterback who they feel is more capable of leading a winning effort, he wasn’t their first choice once Jackson got hurt. Baltimore also tried trading for a different quarterback first, but their negotiations got shut down. Still, who were the Ravens looking to add to the roster? Baltimore Ravens Tried Trading Fourth-Round Pick for Daniel Jones Nov 19, 2026; Houston, Texas, USA; Indianapolis Colts quarterback Daniel Jones (17) looks on from the sideline during the game against the Houston Texans at Reliant Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Troy Taormina-Imagn Images While the Ravens are moving forward with Brissett, according to multiple sources, they also attempted to negotiate a trade with the Indianapolis Colts for Daniel Jones before the Nov. 10 trade deadline expired. The Ravens weren’t the only team to try trading for the former first-round pick, the Minnesota Vikings were reportedly involved too. Yet, the Colts surprised everyone by telling teams that Jones was off-limits in trade discussions. That was a curious decision, considering the Colts released him from the roster 10 days later. Now, according to ESPN’s top NFL insider Adam Schefter , the Ravens offered a fourth-round pick in exchange for Jones and a fifth-round pick. But the trade was conditional. If the Ravens made the playoffs, they’d be sending that fifth-round pick back to the Colts. Nevertheless, the Colts didn’t want to play ball, and they held onto Jones through the deadline before later cutting him loose. “The Ravens offered the Colts a fourth-round draft pick for Daniel Jones and a fifth-round pick, with the condition that the fifth-rounder would be returned to Indianapolis if Baltimore advanced to the playoffs. Minnesota also had interest in Jones. Indy held him, then released him.” Adam Schefter on Daniel Jones Trade Jones is a free agent right now, so if the Ravens are still interested, there’s a chance he could still end up in Baltimore. Yet now that they picked Brissett as the starter, odds are the former No. 6 overall pick will end up elsewhere. Still just 29 years old, there will likely be several teams interested in seeing if they can help get Jones back on track after tossing an NFL-high 13 interceptions thus far. While he likely isn’t looking at another starting role right away, Jones could latch onto a practice squad for the remainder of the season again, much like he did two years ago by joining Kevin O’Connell’s staff in Minnesota. item.title: Roy Keane slams Man Utd fans for applauding players after Liverpool defeat
item.description: Roy Keane slams Man Utd fans for applauding players after Liverpool defeat Roy Keane has hit out at the Manchester United fans applauding the side’s effort in defeat to Liverpool. Manchester United began the Mauricio Pochettino era with a 4-0 defeat to Liverpool at Anfield. A nightmare start saw United reduced to 10 men inside eight minutes when Leny Yoro was sent off for denying a clear goalscoring opportunity, and Liverpool ruthlessly punished the visitors with quick-fire goals from Dominik Szoboszlai and Florian Wirtz. Rio Ngumoha and Victor Munoz added further goals after the interval, as the home side secured an emphatic win. The result piles the pressure on Manchester United, who remain in the Premier League’s relegation places with one win from 11 games. Though large numbers of travelling fans departed Anfield before full-time, Keane questioned the supporters who remained to applaud the side’s effort with 10 men. The former Manchester United captain was confused by any credit for an unacceptable performance. “Has a team ever got a result before with 10 men? It can be done,” Keane said to Sky Sports. “Are you telling me Man Utd couldn’t have done better and everyone is saying it’s not bad. “At least show a bit more fight, a bit more quality, I can’t believe what I’m hearing. Fans are applauding the players, applauding what? Applauding rubbish. “When do the players take responsibility for some of the decision making? Liverpool should have scored eight or nine. I feel like swearing. How can anyone say 4-0 is not too bad? item.title: Hornets Considering Paying Too High A Price For Zion Williamson Trade
item.description: Matthew Hinton-Imagn Images The Charlotte Hornets sit at 4-11 and need a spark, but a proposed trade for Zion Williamson looks like a terrible mistake. The team is desperate for offense after a 111-97 loss in Atlanta on Friday night, yet the cost to get the Pelicans star is simply too high. The Cost of Four Draft Picks The front office pitched the LaMelo deal as a move toward the future, yet this new proposal burns that future for a player with a shaky track record. Yahoo Sports reports that a complete cost analysis indicates paying such a price makes very little sense. Health Concerns and Salary Traps Availability remains the single biggest question mark for any team acquiring the 26-year-old forward. The risk remains massive even though clauses based on games played protect his $42.17 million salary for this season and his $44.89 million deal for 2027-28. Over the course of seven seasons, Williamson has played over just 60 games on only three occasions. The consensus is that he is unable to stay healthy. A Better Path Exists While Bleacher Report suggests “Zion Williamson would give the Hornets a similarly different offensive access point without creating redundancies with any of their core players,” the financial and asset cost is too steep. On the Hoop Collective podcast, ESPN’s Tim MacMahon reported that the Pelicans are unlikely to receive a blockbuster price. “And kind of the consensus that I’ve gotten is, hey, there will be interest in Zion, but there’s not going to be like a blockbuster type of return,” McMahon said. The Hornets should look elsewhere for stability rather than betting the farm on a player who cannot stay on the court.

item.title: Michigan Takes Down UCLA, Ready for Ohio State
item.description: Michigan head coach Kyle Whittingham reacts to a play against UCLA during the second half at Michigan Stadium in Ann Arbor on Saturday, Nov. 21, 2026. Michigan football finally found its footing after a hard-fought win over UCLA . The Wolverines secured a spot in a bowl game with an 18-16 victory in triple overtime. This win at The Big House improved the team’s record to 6-5. But head coach Kyle Whittingham is not looking back at the celebration. His mind is already fixed on the next big challenge. The coaching staff knows the season is far from over. There is only one regular-season game left on the schedule. That final matchup is the annual rivalry against Ohio State. Whittingham knows the stakes are high as the team heads to Columbus. He wants his players to carry the momentum from Saturday forward. Facing a Hostile Road Trip Whittingham has never played inside Ohio Stadium, known as The Shoe. He admits he cannot fully picture the noise until he gets there. “I can envision it. I’ve never been in the Shoe, never played in that stadium,” Whittingham said. Whittingham has faced Ohio State before in a major bowl game. His Utah team met the Buckeyes in the 2022 Rose Bowl, losing a 48-45 shootout. “We did play Ohio State in the Rose Bowl 5 years ago, 4 years ago, so we’ve had a taste of that, and they were … we know they’re a very good football team, very talented,” he added. The coach expects the crowd in Columbus to be loud and angry. He mentioned that Ohio State lost a recent game in Nebraska. “I guess they got beat today in Nebraska, but I think the environment I’m anticipating to be very hostile,” he said. Whittingham has faced tough crowds in his long career. He is not sure if this one will be the worst he has seen, but he is ready to find out. The team must handle the pressure without breaking. Questions About the Coach’s Future While the team celebrates a bowl berth, some fans worry about Whittingham’s job. The season started with high hopes and a roster full of talent. Instead, the team struggled to find a rhythm for most of the year. Insiders at The Athletic reported that some parents of players may have mixed emotions; one said he can “get the program on track if given enough time.” Critics point to specific issues that hurt the team this year. According to The Athletic’s Bruce Feldman and Austin Meek, the offense utilized a “scheme that wasn’t built for the Big Ten.” They also noted a “CEO-style” approach that kept Whittingham too far from the field. Dan Wetzel on the Paul Finebaum Show argued that Whittingham’s legacy is safe despite this year. “Kyle Whittingham as a coach, his legacy is mostly secured. This just, for whatever reason, didn’t gel,” Wetzel stated. The final test will come next week in Ohio. Michigan heads to Columbus for its annual rivalry matchup against Ohio State on November 28. The Wolverines will look to carry the momentum from their win over UCLA into one of the season’s biggest challenges.

item.title: Israel Adesanya’s pre-UFC Saudi Arabia comments called ‘the most concerning interview I’ve ever seen’
item.description: Photo by Chris Unger/Zuffa LLC Chael Sonnen hopes that Israel Adesanya can prove him wrong but has his doubts. On December 5, Israel Adesanya returns in the main event of UFC Saudi Arabia to try and break his four-fight losing streak. Sonnen recently commented on what the former two-time middleweight champion has had to say about how he plans on turning this form around when facing off with Shara Magomedov. Chael Sonnen is rooting for Israel Adesanya but is not convinced by his introspection In a video on his YouTube channel , Israel Adesanya said that he believes he’s been going wrong by trying to prove a point in his fights instead of utilising his best weapon, his mind. This mental shift and leaving his long-time home of City Kickboxing are two changes that ‘The Last Stylebender’ has implemented ahead of his return. Chael Sonnen argued in a video responding to Adesanya’s comments that you can’t think your way to success. He argued that countless fighters have made similar comments in the past but regardless of what changes you make, none of it can replace the hard work required to compete at the highest level. “I’ve seen interviews like this,” he said via his YouTube channel . “I’ve seen a guy that knows he knows the secret. The secret is the mind and he’s re-found himself. I’ve seen these interviews. “I’ve never seen it work out and I will tell you sincerely, I hope for the first time in history it works out and it works out for Izzy. I am a fan, but this interview is easily the most concerning interview that I’ve ever seen.” Sonnen agreed that Adesanya’s fight IQ is a big advantage that he brings to the table. He said that the amount of success the 37-year-old has achieved shows that he’s “the smartest guy in the gym”. With that in mind, Sonnen believes that regardless of Adesanya changing teams, getting back in the win column is something that’s on him. item.title: Pochettino era off to the worst start as new boss makes major blunder that condemns Man United to heavy loss vs Liverpool
item.description: Pochettino era off to the worst start as new boss makes major blunder that condemns Man United to heavy loss vs Liverpool The Mauricio Pochettino era got off to the worst possible start as Manchester United got thrashed 4-0 by Liverpool at Anfield on Sunday. Leny Yoro’s eighth-minute red card changed the complexion of the game completely. It was a naive challenge from the Frenchman, who has looked shaky all season. But the biggest issue on the night was Matthijs de Ligt. He lost his man for the red card and made error after error all night on what was his first Premier League start in almost a year. The Dutchman last played in the league back when Rúben Amorim was in charge. Since then, he has been sidelined with a back injury. Matthijs De Ligt should not have started Former head coach Michael Carrick did not feel the ex-Ajax ace was ready to step up, but Pochettino felt otherwise. And the decision backfired spectacularly. Away at Anfield against a rampaging Liverpool, the new head coach should have gone for the experienced Harry Maguire , who did eventually come on after Yoro’s red card. De Ligt looked like he had lost a yard of pace and could not turn on the ball as quickly, and he was rusty with his passing as well. The damning defeat will show the new boss exactly what a gargantuan task he has on his hands, with the Red Devils languishing in 19th place in the table. Pochettino has a huge task on his hands The action is relentless, with a midweek game coming up against Sporting CP in the Champions League. So time on the training pitch will be limited. The performance on the night was a reminder of how badly INEOS have let standards slip this season. It was clear for all to see that the team needed reinforcements at the back in the summer, but the co-owners opted to ignore it and revamp only the midfield. With relegation a very real possibility, INEOS must spend in January to help the new head coach. Otherwise, things could get murky very soon. Feature image Michael Regan via Getty Images

item.title: Watch Chris Berman’s emotional tribute to Tom Jackson: ‘All of us are stunned’
item.description: Watch Chris Berman’s emotional tribute to Tom Jackson: ‘All of us are stunned’ originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Chris Berman and Tom Jackson were synonymous with football at ESPN, so it's only fitting that Berman got to honor Jackson on Sunday. Jackson died at the age of 75 on Friday, but Berman and the rest of ESPN didn't announce the news until Sunday. While Berman is no longer the host of "Sunday NFL Countdown," he joined the current crew to honor Jackson, who was such an integral part of the show for multiple decades. While Jackson was no longer working at ESPN, his impact is clear in the way that current ESPN analysts speak about him. Instead of previewing today's slate of games, ESPN honored Jackson for much of the show to open the three-hour broadcast. Watch Berman and the "NFL Sunday Countdown" analysts honor Jackson. MORE : Football world mourns loss of Tom Jackson Chris Berman, 'NFL Sunday Countdown' honors Tom Jackson To open "NFL Sunday Countdown" on Sunday, Chris Berman broke the news that his friend and former partner Tom Jackson died. "It was unexpected," Berman said. "He was a vital 75. Tom was poignant; he was active. This is a shock." Berman went on to say that he had just spoken with Jackson several times over the past week, and that the two would always talk about more than just football. Berman held back tears as he honored his "best friend," whom he won't be able to speak with anymore. Berman put out an official statement through ESPN that he read on air to wrap up his time honoring Jackson. "All of us are stunned. I'm stunned; we all here at 'Countdown' and ESPN are stunned," he said. "We've lost one of the best human beings to ever walk the planet, Tom Jackson...Tom was so much more than an accomplished NFL analyst. While the course has been open for play in recent weeks, much of it is sodden and muddy, even causing some drives in the fairway to plug into the ground. Some areas have suffered significant damage from apparent golf-cart traffic, while sections along the Intracoastal bear scars left by receding water. Nicklaus, who was honored as part of an American Free Enterprise event at Palm Beach Atlantic in West Palm Beach on Nov. 17, has become one of the sport’s most acclaimed golf-course designers. He has personally designed 325 courses and remains active in establishing "Nicklaus Design." item.title: Dylan Larkin Gives Up Over 7 Figures Waiting for Red Wings Trade
item.description: Dylan Larkin Red Wings Getty Former Detroit Red Wings captain Dylan Larkin has given up over seven figures in forfeited salary while he awaits a trade. Larkin asked the Red Wings for a trade in the summer, but the team held onto him, and he came to training camp with the team. After playing in a handful of games with Detroit, he decided to step away from the team on October 29. He has been suspended since then and is losing $41,000 per day in forfeited salary. Dylan Larkin Has Given Up $1 Million in Salary On Sunday, Larkin’s forfeited salary topped the $1 million mark, per Helene St. James of the Detroit Free Press. “The former Detroit Red Wings captain now has topped $1 million in forfeited salary since he had his agent inform the team he ‘no longer wants to be a Red Wing’ on Oct. 29, at which point the Wings changed his status to suspended without pay. Larkin, from Waterford, is forfeiting just north of $41,000 a day. That Larkin would leave so much money on the table – true, his career earnings already top $66 million, not bad for a 30-year-old – speaks to resolve in wanting what he asked for shortly after last season ended in April: A trade away from his hometown NHL team, the one that drafted him No. 15 in 2014, and of which he served as captain from January 2021 until this past offseason,” St. James wrote. When Will the Red Wings Trade Dylan Larkin? The Red Wings seem to be wanting to wait for the perfect trade to send Larkin away . As of yet, they have not gotten the trade package that they want to deal him, but as the clock continues to tick, the team really needs to think about dealing their top trade asset and stop being so picky with what sort of trade offers they get back, as Larkin sitting on the sidelines isn’t good for anyone. The NHL trade deadline is on March 1, so the Red Wings still have a lot of time left, but for the sake of both the player and the team, it would be better to trade him ASAP. The Crew turned the boat around, going from worst in the Eastern Conference to closing the season on a six-game win streak and having won eight of their last nine. That was enough not only to jump out of Thursday’s wild card match but to set up a First Round playoff series with Inter Miami, the reigning champion led by Lionel Messi. They also pushed to the U.S. Open Cup final, falling to St. Louis City in a penalty shootout. All of it led Tall to believe he made the right decisions, moving on quickly from the coach he thought was the right man for the job. “Some people could’ve waited the full year. Maybe it would’ve been safer, but that’s not me. That’s not us as a club. That’s not even the way we play!” Tall told USA TODAY Sports ahead of the playoffs. “You see how we are bold and are not afraid of taking risk. At the end of the day, it wasn’t even a risk necessarily. It was necessary for our players, for our club as a whole and I think ultimately we made the right decision to do it at that time.” Tall still stands by Rydström as a good coach, something he’s proving while leading Hammarby in Sweden which currently sits atop of the table after running off five consecutive wins. But he wasn’t the right fit for the Crew in the post-Nancy era. The Crew turned to Courtois, a former Crew academy and MLS Next Pro coach who continued the idea first expressed on the field so successfully by Nancy’s teams. item.title: Gotham FC’s title defense comes to crushing end in semifinal loss after venue change
item.description: They came by car, by the special-event X80 bus, by bike if they were feeling sporty. They came in layers, in beanies and scarves, with Gotham’s black-and-sky-blue colors on top. They came on behalf of those who couldn’t come, capacity being reduced at this impromptu change of venue, each one trying to make noise for five. Gotham FC forward Sam Kerr (20) competes for the ball against Kansas City Current defender Gabrielle Robinson (24) on Sunday, Nov. 15, 2026, in New York City. IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect They came with some measure of outrage — these home-field shenanigans would never happen in men’s sports — while their better angels told them to come in joy, in celebration, everyone watching women’s sports. And then, 25 miles and 20,000 seats removed from their regular destination at New Jersey’s Sports Illustrated Stadium, huddled in the bleachers by a blue track ringing an immaculate pitch at Icahn Stadium on Randall’s Island, in the shadow of the old Psychiatric Center and with the light fading over the Costco across the river, 5,000 devoted souls Sunday afternoon watched Gotham’s NWSL title defense end in a 2-1 semifinal loss to the Kansas City Current. “We lost today because we weren’t the better team,” Gotham winger and oracle Midge Purce said. “That being said, I would say it’s inexcusable. It’s not what you want in a professional league. It’s not what you want for women who are progressing in the United States and supposed to be one of the best leagues in the entire world. I think it’s a bad look for everyone involved. And we always want to be at Sports Illustrated in front of our fans when we earned that right throughout the season. But I would say it had no effect on performance today.” The match had been moved to Icahn on Monday due to concerns over the disintegrating field conditions at Sports Illustrated, which had unfortunately overshadowed Gotham’s quarterfinal victory there last weekend. Gotham was unbeaten in its past 13 matches at Sports Illustrated, which is operated by the Red Bulls of MLS. item.title: Beckham to be inducted into US Soccer Hall of Fame
item.description: David Beckham was knighted by King Charles in 2025 [Getty Images] David Beckham will be inducted into the United States' National Soccer Hall of Fame as part of its 2027 class. The former Manchester United and England midfielder, 51, made headlines in 2007 when he moved to Los Angeles from Spanish giants Real Madrid to join Major League Soccer (MLS) side LA Galaxy on a five-year contract. He made 124 appearances in all competitions for Galaxy, scoring 20 goals, and twice won both the MLS Cup and Supporters' Shield. Beckham's six seasons at Galaxy helped to raise the global profile of MLS and following his retirement in 2013, he became co-owner of MLS club Inter Miami, who signed Argentina World Cup winner Lionel Messi in 2023. His induction ceremony is set to take place on 16 April 2027 in Frisco, Texas. David Beckham's deal with LA Galaxy in 2007 was reportedly worth £128m [Getty Images] He was told the news he had been chosen on the veterans' ballot at an MLS board of governors' meeting on Thursday and said his time in the US has been "an incredible journey". Beckham, who had two loan spells with AC Milan in 2009 and 2010 while at Galaxy, added: "I'm looking to build this league and this sport in this great country for a long time." Meanwhile, former US internationals Megan Rapinoe and Julie Ertz have also been voted into the Hall of Fame in their first year of eligibility. Ballon d'Or winner Rapinoe, 41, and midfielder Ertz, 34, lifted the Women’s World Cup twice with with the US in 2015 and 2019. "To be alongside all the greatest players that have played for us, and played for our country alongside a bunch of my team-mates and friends, recognised like that in this way just means you were successful and a part of great teams," Rapinoe wrote on Instagram. item.description: Seattle Reign FC defender Phoebe McClernon, left, defends Gotham FC forward Guro Reiten during an NWSL playoff game in Harrison, N.J., Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026. For the first time in franchise history, Gotham FC is set to host its semifinal match next weekend. But there’s an unfortunate twist. Gotham’s semifinal match against the Kansas City Current won’t be played at the club’s typical stomping grounds in Harrison, New Jersey. Instead, Gotham agreed to move Sunday’s match to Icahn Stadium on Randall’s Island for better playing surface quality. “This was an extremely difficult decision, and one we did not take lightly,” Gotham president of soccer operations Yael Averbuch West said in a letter to fans. “After thoughtful consultation with coach Juan Carlos Amorós, our team captains, and our ownership, we felt it was important to prioritize a playing surface that appropriately allows our athletes to perform at their best. item.title: Messi makes history with MLS Golden Boot
item.description: Messi retired from international football with Argentina earlier this year [Getty Images] Inter Miami forward Lionel Messi has become the first player in MLS history to win the Golden Boot in consecutive seasons. The eight-time Ballon d'Or winner scored 26 goals in 31 appearances, four clear of FC Dallas striker Peter Musa and five more than Nashville's English forward Sam Surridge. Messi becomes only the sixth player to land the award twice, joining a list that includes former Charlton Athletic and Southampton striker Bradley Wright-Phillips. In addition to his goals, the 39-year-old notched 17 assists over the course of the MLS season, ensuring his 43 goal contributions was also a league best for the second year in a row. And the World Cup winner could soon make more history as he bids to become the first three-time Landon Donovan MLS MVP winner. The former Argentina forward landed the award in 2024 as Inter Miami won the Supporters' Shield title and also in 2025 as they won the MLS Cup. Despite Messi's magic, Miami weren't able to land top spot in the MLS Eastern Conference, with the team finishing 17 points behind Surridge's Nashville. They will now face Columbus Crew over three games in the first round of the MLS Cup play-offs which begin later this month. item.title: On MLS Decision Day, D.C. United faces a familiar reality: Another season of failure
item.description: WASHINGTON — All around Major League Soccer , from Montreal to Miami and Seattle to San Diego, Saturday was Decision Day — the last act in an 8½-month production. While three playoff berths were in the balance, teams with guaranteed spots sought to improve their place. It's a day marked by desperation, scoreboard-watching and playoff-planning. At Audi Field, however, Decision Day felt more like Derision Day. For the seventh consecutive year, D.C. United, once a showpiece of a blossoming league, has no playoff plans — a near impossibility in a league that distributes postseason passes like a guy on a New York street corner handing out flyers for discount mattresses. Only Toronto FC's eight-year rut, starting with its 2007 expansion campaign, lasted longer. United wasn't even in the mix on Decision Day, its fate having been decided 10 days earlier. The lowly finale was against another failed side, New York City FC, which claimed a 1-0 victory on a late goal. While 2026 was an anomaly for the New Yorkers, it was the norm in the nation's capital. D.C. added another sad chapter to a rotten story under an ownership group, led by Jason Levien and Steve Kaplan, that has dragged the organization into irrelevance in not just the prospering league but in the local market and the ascending sport. The public-address announcer introduces the team as "your four-time MLS Cup champions," but he's been saying that for a long time. Given the league's evolution, it feels even longer. United's last title, in 2004, came in a 10-team operation — one-third the current landscape. Since then, 13 different clubs have hoisted the trophy. Less than two miles north of Audi Field, the U.S. Capitol witnessed a historic sea change Tuesday with a political wave that swept the ruling party out of office. Local soccer fans have had no such luck with those in power at Audi Field. Under the current regime … United hasn't won a playoff game in 11 years and hasn't advanced to the conference finals in 14. Twelve years have passed since it won at least half its 34 matches. United's only trophy in recent memory was the 2013 U.S. Open Cup, which came amid a horrific, three-win regular season. D.C. is on its fourth head coach since Ben Olsen's departure in late 2020 and its second head of soccer operations in four years. The current director, Erkut Sogut — an agent best known for representing former German star Mesut Özil — was hired last fall without any experience working for a team. Another goal conceded, another season to forget. Keisuke Kurokawa's frustration summed up D.C. United's latest disappointing chapter. Scott Taetsch via Getty Images United remains one of three MLS organizations without a developmental team bridging the youth academy to the first team.
